question: High growth rate with use of modern technology and self-reliance of the economy could be achieved only if:

options.text: benefits of economic prosperity reach the poor people
benefits of economic prosperity reach the rich people
the economy participates in international trade

solution:
The correct answer is__** benefits of economic prosperity reach the poor people.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The **most effective means** of** eradicating poverty** and **raising the standards of living** in developing nations is** economic growth.**
 
• It is obvious **how growth and decreasing poverty** are positively correlated.
 
• It is less clear how th**e income distribution affects this relationship,** specifically whether greater** inequality diminishes** the **decrease in poverty** brought on by growth.
 
• The degree to which income** inequality exists** at the outset affects how **well growth reduces poverty.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Supply-side economics, new classical economics, monetarism, and Keynesian economics** are the four main economic theories.
 
• **Supply-side Economics:**
 
 
• The law of supply and demand establishes the **economic relationship between producers and consumers** of various commodities.
 
• According to the principle of **supply and demand**, a product's price is influenced by both its** accessibility and consumer desire.**
 
 
 
• **classical new economics:**
 
 
• The main school of economic theory in the **18th and 19th centuries** is referred to by the term** "classical economics,"**
 
• Most people credit Scottish economist** Adam Smith as the creator **of classical economic theory
 
 
 
• **Monetarism:**
 
 
• The foundation of monetarism is the **quantity theory of money.**
 
• It claims that the** nominal expenditures of the economy **are equal to the money supply times velocity.
 
 
 
• **Keynesian economics:**
 
 
• In his General Theory of** Employment, Interest, and Money, John Maynard Keynes **put forth a number of theories (1935-36)
